evidence_records.publication_title: Combined Nivolumab and Ipilimumab or Monotherapy in Untreated Melanoma
evidence_records.trial_population: 945 previously untreated adults with unresectable stageIII/IV melanoma; ECOG 0–1.
evidence_records.intervention: Nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV q 3 weeks ×4, then nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV q 2 weeks.
evidence_records.comparator: Ipilimumab 3 mg/kg q 3 weeks ×4 and a separate nivolumab 3 mg/kg q 2 weeks arm.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Co-primary PFS and OS; this publication reports the primary PFS analysis.
evidence_records.analysis_timepoint: Original 2015 analysis, not final 10-year OS analysis.
key_findings: Median PFS: combination 11.5 months (95%CI 8.9–16.7), ipilimumab 2.9 months (2.8–3.4), nivolumab 6.9 months (4.3–9.5).
Combination versus ipilimumab: progression/death HR 0.42 (99.5%CI 0.31–0.57; P<0.001). This interval is 99.5%, not 95%.
Grade 3–4 treatment-related adverse events at this analysis:55.0% combination,16.3% nivolumab,27.3% ipilimumab.
limitations: The planned statistical comparisons were against ipilimumab; a superiority claim over nivolumab alone is not supported by a powered direct comparison.
Historical weight-based IV maintenance differs from current NCCP fixed IV/SC choices.
Trial ECOG 0–1 does not replace current NCCPv 11 eligibility 0–2; evidence in ECOG 2 is less direct.
evidence_records.review_status: Primary sources reconciled; independent consultant and oncology pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.publication_title: Final, 10-Year Outcomes with Nivolumab plus Ipilimumab in Advanced Melanoma
evidence_records.study_design: Final follow-up of the same randomised phase 3 population
evidence_records.trial_population: 945 patients: combination 314, nivolumab 316, ipilimumab 315; previously untreated advanced melanoma.
evidence_records.intervention: Original nivolumab 1/ipilimumab 3 induction and weight-based IV nivolumab maintenance.
evidence_records.comparator: Ipilimumab control; nivolumab-alone arm retained for descriptive comparison.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: OS and PFS were co-primary; melanoma-specific survival was post hoc.
evidence_records.analysis_timepoint: Database lock 16 May 2024; minimum 120 months since last randomisation. Published online 15 September 2024, journal issue 2 January 2025.
key_findings: Median OS:71.9 months combination,36.9 months nivolumab,19.9 months ipilimumab.
Ten-year OS estimates:43% combination,37% nivolumab,19% ipilimumab.
limitations: Combination versus nivolumab comparisons remain descriptive; the study was not powered for that formal comparison.
These are population OS estimates, not an individual prognosis, cure rate or HCC/adjuvant benefit.
Do not mix post-hoc melanoma-specific survival with overall survival.
Current IV/SC schedules are not the literal regimen studied in 2013–14.
evidence_records.review_status: Primary sources reconciled; independent consultant and oncology pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.publication_title: Long-term outcomes of patients with active melanoma brain metastases treated with combination nivolumab plus ipilimumab: final phase 2 results
evidence_records.trial_population: 101 asymptomatic patients (ECOG 0–1, no baseline steroids) and 18 symptomatic patients (ECOG 0–2, stable symptoms; low-dose dexamethasone allowed).
evidence_records.intervention: Nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg q 3 weeks ×4, then nivolumab 3 mg/kg q 2 weeks for up to 2 years.
evidence_records.comparator: No randomised control; cohorts are clinically different.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Investigator-assessed intracranial clinical benefit; intracranial PFS and OS secondary.
evidence_records.analysis_timepoint: Final 3-year follow-up; median follow-up 34.3 months asymptomatic and 7.5 months symptomatic.
key_findings: Intracranial clinical benefit:57.4% (58/101) asymptomatic and 16.7% (3/18) symptomatic.
This supports selected CNS-context discussion; it does not establish a randomised benefit between symptom cohorts.
limitations: Do not apply asymptomatic-cohort rates to symptomatic or corticosteroid-dependent patients.
The smaller symptomatic cohort and shorter follow-up constrain interpretation.
Does not override NCCP symptomatic-CNS caution or create a melanoma 24 month treatment cap.
evidence_records.review_status: Primary sources reconciled; independent consultant and oncology pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.publication_title: PD-1 Blockade with Cemiplimab in Advanced Cutaneous Squamous-Cell Carcinoma
evidence_records.study_design: Open-label single-arm phase 2 metastatic cohort; separate phase 1 expansion also reported
evidence_records.trial_population: 59 patients in the pivotal metastatic-CSCC cohort; do not merge with the 26-patient phase 1 cohort.
evidence_records.intervention: Cemiplimab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks; response assessments every 8 weeks.
evidence_records.analysis_timepoint: Original phase 2 metastatic analysis; median follow-up 7.9 months.
key_findings: Among 28 responders,57% had an observed response duration>6 months at the cutoff.
Treatment discontinued because of adverse events in 7% of the metastatic cohort.
limitations: Single-arm response does not establish comparative survival, cure or benefit over surgery/radiotherapy.
The dose was 3 mg/kg q 2 weeks, not current NCCP 350 mg q 3 weeks.
Use the separate locally advanced cohort and exact fixed-dose cohort when discussing those settings.
No cervical or adjuvant-CSCC benefit is inferred.
evidence_records.review_status: Primary sources reconciled; independent consultant and oncology pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.publication_title: Cemiplimab in locally advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma: results from an open-label, phase 2, single-arm trial
evidence_records.trial_population: 78 adults with locally advanced CSCC, ECOG 0–1, not candidates for curative surgery/radiotherapy.
evidence_records.intervention: Cemiplimab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks for up to 96 weeks.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Independent central response using integrated radiology/photography criteria.
key_findings: Independent response:34/78,44% (95%CI 32–55), comprising 10 complete and 24 partial responses.
Grade 3–4 treatment-emergent adverse events:34/78(44%); this is all-cause TEAE, not treatment-related toxicity.
One treatment-related death followed aspiration pneumonia.
limitations: Single-arm cohort; no comparative survival estimate.
Trial ECOG 0–1 and exclusion criteria limit extrapolation to broader NCCP-eligible patients.
Historical weight-based schedule; do not label this as direct 350 mgq 3 weeks cohort evidence.
evidence_records.review_status: Primary sources reconciled; independent consultant and oncology pharmacy review pending

evidence_records.publication_title: Phase 2 study of cemiplimab in metastatic cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma: primary analysis of fixed-dosing, long-term outcome of weight-based dosing
evidence_records.trial_population: 56 adults with nodal/distant metastatic CSCC, ECOG 0–1 and measurable disease.
evidence_records.intervention: Cemiplimab 350 mg IV over 30 minutes every 3 weeks; initial planned 54 weeks, option to extend 96 weeks.
evidence_records.comparator: None; the separately enrolled 3 mg/kg cohort is not a randomised comparator.
evidence_records.primary_endpoint: Independent-central-review objective response, evaluated independently by cohort.
evidence_records.analysis_timepoint: Primary fixed-dose analysis; median follow-up 8.1 months (range 0.6–14.1).
key_findings: Independent response:23/56,41.1% (95%CI 28.1–55.0), comprising 3 complete and 20 partial responses.
Median duration of response was not reached at this early analysis.
limitations: Exact current NCCP dose/interval cohort, but metastatic disease only.
Do not substitute investigator ORR 51.8% for independent ORR 41.1%.
Do not use the updated weight-based group 1 ORR 49.2% as the fixed-dose result.
No comparative survival or adjuvant benefit can be calculated from this single-arm cohort.
Study transplant exclusion differs from NCCP CSCC transplant caution; evidence is limited in transplant recipients.
evidence_records.review_status: Primary sources reconciled; independent consultant and oncology pharmacy review pending
